question: One frozen checkpoint: allocate complete-request time to loops versus Euler steps.

fixed.sampler: Euler, original torch.linspace float32 grid, original x0-to-velocity clamp_min(.05)
fixed.encoder_dtype: original from_pretrained default, measured before forward
fixed.initial_noise: CUDA BF16 torch.randn with per-request dedicated CUDA generator then multiply noise_scale; hash before write-back; noise same across all L/S for pair

latency_dev.method: Least-squares straight line across the three DEV step counts, round nearest integer, clip to allowed range, verify on all three DEV prompts. If outside measured grid mark extrapolated. No further grid search; if >5% mismatch retain nearest actually measured setting and report quality-time, not exact equal-time.

data.noise_seed: seed_label + 100000*prompt_index; stable mapping frozen in job manifest

budget.includes: pilot, warmup, parity, diagnostics, DEV, MAIN and repeat timing; failed starts are charged

evaluation.primary: all-constraint pass rate C_time minus A_time
evaluation.independent_clusters: 16 prompts; four related template families are a further dependence limitation
evaluation.quantile: numpy.quantile method=linear, 2.5/97.5 percentiles, descriptive 95% paired prompt-cluster interval
evaluation.uncertain: failure for primary; count plus all-uncertain-as-pass sensitivity separate
evaluation.timing: warmed string-to-tokenization/T5/sampling/CPU-PIL complete; cold load, PNG write, evaluator/profiler excluded; sampler-only CUDA event excludes text encode and initial noise construction
